title: 1980 AHSME Problem 9
statement: A man walks \(x\) miles due west, turns \(150^\circ\) to his left and walks \(3\) miles in the new direction. If he finishes at a point \(\sqrt3\) miles from his starting point, then \(x\) is

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
not uniquely determined by the given
information

solutions.text:
Take east as the positive horizontal direction. After the turn, the \(3\)-mile displacement has components \((\frac{3\sqrt3}{2},-\frac{3}{2}).\) Therefore \[ \left(\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}-x\right)^2 +\left(\frac32\right)^2=3. \] Hence \(\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}-x=\pm\frac{\sqrt3}{2},\) giving \(x=\sqrt3\) or \(x=2\sqrt3.\) The value is not unique.

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
hints: Resolve the second walk into horizontal and vertical components
The distance equation is quadratic in \(x\); check whether both positive roots are valid
